title: TCS Named a Leader in Everest Group's Agentic Process Automation Assessment
excerpt: Everest Group's 2026 APA PEAK Matrix assessed 26 providers and placed TCS among seven Leaders, citing its WisdomNext, ignio and Cognitive Automation platforms.
body:
• Everest Group's Agentic Process Automation (APA) Solutions PEAK Matrix 2026 places TCS among seven Leaders, in an assessment covering 26 solution providers.
  • The report cites TCS's proprietary stack — AI WisdomNext, the ignio AIOps platform and the TCS Cognitive Automation Platform — behind its "Autonomous GBS" pitch for AI-led business operations.
  • The recognition lands as large employers shift from automating individual tasks to AI agents that execute whole processes, with humans in oversight and governance roles.

Tata Consultancy Services has been named a Leader in Everest Group's Agentic Process Automation (APA) Solutions PEAK Matrix, the company announced on October 26. Everest Group's assessment covered 26 APA solution providers and placed seven in the Leaders quadrant: Accenture, Capgemini, Cognizant, HCLTech, IBM, PwC and TCS, according to the assessment extract published by Everest Group.

What Everest Group credited

According to TCS's summary of the report, Everest Group pointed to the company's vision of autonomous, AI-driven business operations — an "Autonomous Global Business Services" (GBS) model built on process reimagination rather than task-by-task automation. The report highlighted a portfolio of proprietary offerings: TCS AI WisdomNext, which consolidates generative and agentic AI services into a unified interface; ignio, its AIOps platform; and the TCS Cognitive Automation Platform, which connects legacy systems with modern automation.

"Agentic AI is ushering in a new operating paradigm where enterprises move beyond automating tasks to building autonomous, self-optimizing business operations."

— Akhilesh Tiwari, Head, Autonomous Business Operations, TCS

Tiwari said TCS is helping organizations move toward AI-led operations "where intelligent agents execute, learn, and adapt at scale while humans provide strategic oversight, governance, and judgement," and that the recognition reinforces the company's push to turn operations into "intelligent, outcome-centric engines."

Why the category matters

Agentic process automation is the enterprise-software industry's current centre of gravity: instead of software that follows fixed rules, AI agents are given goals — process an insurance claim, reconcile invoices, triage IT incidents — and execute multi-step workflows, escalating to humans on exceptions. For India's IT services majors, the category is strategically loaded. Their traditional business sells skilled labour by the hour; agentic automation sells outcomes, and every large provider is racing to prove its platforms, not just its headcount, can run a client's operations.

The timing is also pointed. Earlier this month, TCS was one of six IT services firms suspended from the US PERM green card sponsorship program amid a federal enforcement push — a reminder of how exposed the old labour-arbitrage model is to immigration politics. Recognition in the APA category speaks to the other side of that ledger: TCS's argument to clients and investors that its growth engine is shifting from moving people to deploying AI agents. Whether that shift protects margins as clients automate work they once outsourced is the open question the next few earnings seasons will answer.

The APA recognition is the latest in a run of Everest Group Leader placements for TCS this year, including multi-process human resources outsourcing in October and banking IT services in June — a pattern the company uses in enterprise sales cycles, where analyst shortlists often decide which vendors are invited to bid. Everest Group's PEAK Matrix assessments grade providers on market impact and on vision and capability, and placement is widely cited across the industry in pursuit of large transformation deals.
